WTI crude futures were quoted at $97.25 per barrel, compared with their previous settlement of $96.46, representing an increase of $0.79, or approximately 0.82%. Both benchmarks remained below the levels recorded before Monday's sharp decline. Exact quotation time was not independently established. These figures are not final settlements. Intraday high and low figures have been omitted because a consistent, timestamp-matched dataset could not be verified. What Happened to Brent and WTI Today? Crude oil markets experienced significant price movements across the first two trading sessions of November. On Monday, November 2, Brent settled at $104.77 per barrel after declining $8.66, or 7.63%. WTI settled at $96.46 per barrel after a decline of approximately 7.4%. The movements followed developments surrounding diplomatic efforts to end the conflict involving Iran. Reports indicated that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had discussed progress towards negotiations with the United States. However, reports of further US military activity involving Iran's Qeshm Island introduced additional uncertainty surrounding shipping and energy infrastructure near the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is a strategically important maritime route for international oil shipments. Disruptions to commercial shipping can affect tanker availability, freight costs, delivery schedules and the perceived risk of supply interruptions. Tuesday's partial price recovery occurred as markets continued assessing the implications of both diplomatic and military developments. What Is the Difference Between Brent and WTI? Brent and WTI are two widely followed international crude oil benchmarks. Brent is a major reference for oil traded across international markets, including crude sourced from Europe, Africa and parts of the Middle East. WTI is a US crude oil benchmark associated with production and pricing in North America. Differences in crude quality, transportation infrastructure, delivery locations and regional market conditions contribute to the price difference between the benchmarks. At the reported November 3 quotations, Brent traded at a premium of $8.30 per barrel over WTI. Why Do Crude Oil Prices Matter for India? India's Import Bill India relies heavily on imported crude oil to meet domestic petroleum requirements. For unchanged import quantities, higher dollar-denominated crude prices increase the value of imported oil. Lower prices have the opposite arithmetic effect. The eventual rupee cost also depends on exchange rates, freight charges, crude grade and procurement terms. Inflation Crude oil is a major input in petroleum products, transportation and several industrial processes. Changes in crude costs can affect petrol, diesel, aviation turbine fuel, freight and petrochemical production costs. The extent and timing of transmission to consumer prices depend on retail pricing mechanisms, taxes, inventories and commercial arrangements. Airlines and Logistics Aviation turbine fuel is an important operating expense for airlines. Changes in international crude prices can influence aviation fuel procurement costs, subject to refining economics and domestic fuel pricing. Road transportation businesses are similarly exposed to diesel costs through fleet operations and freight contracts. These cost mechanisms do not establish a particular direction for the share prices of airline or logistics companies. Paints, Chemicals and Manufacturing Crude oil and natural gas derivatives are important inputs in paints, packaging, plastics, synthetic materials and chemical manufacturing. Changes in petroleum feedstock prices can affect production costs, input inventories and procurement requirements. The ultimate financial impact depends on pricing contracts, raw-material mixes, inventory turnover and the ability to pass through costs. Refiners and Oil-Marketing Companies Refineries process crude oil into petroleum products such as petrol, diesel and aviation fuel. Their economics depend on the difference between crude acquisition costs and the value of refined products, alongside operating expenses. Therefore, movements in crude prices must be assessed together with refining margins, product prices, inventories and domestic retail pricing. Upstream Oil Producers Companies involved in crude oil exploration and production generally receive revenue linked to realised crude prices and production volumes. However, realised prices may differ from Brent and WTI benchmarks because of contractual terms, crude quality and other adjustments. Rupee and External Balance Crude oil imports are largely priced in US dollars. For a given import volume and exchange rate, higher international crude prices increase the dollar value of oil imports. Changes in the import bill can influence India's merchandise trade deficit and current-account position, alongside movements in other trade and income components.

articles.title: Diwali rally continues: Sensex surges 1,225 points, Nifty gains 1.58% on FII inflows
articles.description: New Delhi: Indian stock markets extended their winning streak on Tuesday, November 3, with the Sensex surging over 1,225 points and the Nifty gaining 1.58 per cent as falling crude oil prices, renewed foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows and encouraging corporate earnings fuelled the pre-Diwali rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed 1,225.07 points, or 1.62 per cent, to settle at 76,917.85, while the NSE Nifty 50 advanced 370.05 points, or 1.58 per cent, to close at 23,810.85. The rally marked the fourth consecutive session of gains for benchmark indices, with the Sensex adding 2,458.32 points over Monday and Tuesday alone, offering investors a strong start to Diwali week. The rebound was supported by foreign institutional investors returning to Indian equities after sustained selling. FIIs purchased shares worth approximately Rs 3,115 crore on Monday, providing fresh momentum to the domestic market. A sharp correction in international crude oil prices further boosted sentiment by easing concerns over India's import bill, inflation and pressure on the rupee. Brent crude was trading around USD 105.71 per barrel at the time of reporting. FMCG, realty and banking stocks lead gains Buying was particularly strong in consumer-focused sectors, with Nifty FMCG emerging as the biggest sectoral gainer, rising 3.18 per cent. Nifty Realty advanced 2.10 per cent, followed by Nifty Private Bank at 1.77 per cent and Nifty Auto at 1.47 per cent. Nifty Media also ended 0.49 per cent higher. However, the rally was not uniform across sectors. Nifty PSU Bank declined 1.37 per cent, Nifty Metal fell 0.40 per cent and Nifty IT slipped 0.15 per cent. Major gainers and losers Nestle India, Tata Consumer Products and Asian Paints were among the prominent gainers, reflecting strong buying interest in consumption-oriented stocks. BSE Ltd also featured among the notable winners in the broader market. On the losing side, Power Grid, State Bank of India, ONGC, Adani Enterprises, Tata Steel and NTPC faced selling pressure. Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, attributed the sustained recovery to falling crude prices, easing US Treasury yields and renewed foreign investor participation. He said resilient second-quarter corporate earnings had strengthened confidence in India's domestic growth outlook, while fresh institutional inflows supported broader market participation. However, Nair cautioned that the sustainability of the rally would depend on corporate earnings, continued foreign investment and further moderation in oil prices. Rupee strengthens, gold and silver decline The positive sentiment extended to the currency market, with the Indian rupee strengthening against the US dollar on Tuesday. The domestic currency ended around 94.74 against the dollar, compared with its previous close of 94.90. Meanwhile, precious metals continued their downward trend ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali. Gold prices declined 1.26 per cent to Rs 1,38,420 per 10 grams for 24-karat gold, while silver fell 3.59 per cent to Rs 1,77,120 per kg. Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research at Brickwork Ratings, said the steep fall in crude prices had provided immediate relief to the currency market. He noted that Brent crude had fallen nearly 6.5 per cent to around USD 106 per barrel, easing one of the biggest macroeconomic pressures on the Indian economy. However, a relatively firm US dollar and uncertainty surrounding the US midterm elections limited the rupee's appreciation. Asian markets remain under pressure The strong performance of Indian equities contrasted with weakness across several Asian markets. Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 0.33 per cent, while South Korea's KOSPI and Taiwan's Weighted Index each dropped 3.72 per cent. Singapore's Straits Times fell 0.66 per cent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the regional trend with a 0.39 per cent gain. Market participants will now monitor foreign investment flows, crude oil movements, upcoming corporate earnings and the US Federal Reserve's policy outlook for indications of whether the rally can continue through Diwali week.

Road transportation businesses are similarly exposed to diesel costs through fleet operations and freight contracts. These cost mechanisms do not establish a particular direction for the share prices of airline or logistics companies. Paints, Chemicals and Manufacturing Crude oil and natural gas derivatives are important inputs in paints, packaging, plastics, synthetic materials and chemical manufacturing. Changes in petroleum feedstock prices can affect production costs, input inventories and procurement requirements. The ultimate financial impact depends on pricing contracts, raw-material mixes, inventory turnover and the ability to pass through costs. Refiners and Oil-Marketing Companies Refineries process crude oil into petroleum products such as petrol, diesel and aviation fuel. Their economics depend on the difference between crude acquisition costs and the value of refined products, alongside operating expenses. Therefore, movements in crude prices must be assessed together with refining margins, product prices, inventories and domestic retail pricing. Upstream Oil Producers Companies involved in crude oil exploration and production generally receive revenue linked to realised crude prices and production volumes. However, realised prices may differ from Brent and WTI benchmarks because of contractual terms, crude quality and other adjustments. Rupee and External Balance Crude oil imports are largely priced in US dollars. For a given import volume and exchange rate, higher international crude prices increase the dollar value of oil imports. Changes in the import bill can influence India's merchandise trade deficit and current-account position, alongside movements in other trade and income components.

articles.title: Two arrested in Eastern Cape for impersonating IEC official
articles.description: Two arrested in Eastern Cape for impersonating IEC official Nokuthula Khanyile Tue, 11/03/2026 - 12:30 GQEBERHA - Two people have been arrested in the Eastern Cape for allegedly impersonating an Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) official. It is alleged that at about 4.30am on 2 November 2026, the suspects arrived at Ngcobo Police Station to collect voting material, claiming they had been sent by the presiding officer. However, the presiding officer was already at the station and had not authorised anyone to collect the material. READ | Two arrested in Limpopo for election-related offences The suspects were identified before leaving the station, and the voting material was confiscated. Both have been arrested and are being processed. Eastern Cape Provincial Commissioner Lieutenant General Vuyisile Ncata condemned the incident, stating that any attempt to interfere with the electoral process would not be tolerated. “We will not tolerate any interference with the electoral process. The arrest of the two suspects demonstrates our commitment to upholding the integrity of the elections. Anyone who impersonates an IEC official will face the full might of the law,” said Ncata.
